Hope you're well. We're getting our FY28 cloud spend lined up and look to increase our committed capacity with Redwood on the GCP marketplace. A few asks from procurement:

Thanks for the ping. Quick operational notes after reviewing Jordan's PO and the requested uplift:

- Capacity mapping: The 40% committed uplift looks like a mix of burstable and on-demand vCPU SKU groups across us-central1 and us-east1. To preserve latency SLAs we recommend pinning the committed units to specific SKU families (n1-standard / n2-standard) and adding a capped burst allowance.
- Term model: GCP private offers support custom term lengths; the 18-month term is doable but will need explicit start/end dates on the offer.
- Billing cadence: GCP's marketplace typically issues monthly invoices from the vendor; to meet Acme's quarterly internal cadence we can either (a) keep monthly invoices and provide a quarterly consolidated statement, or (b) set expectations in the PO that Redwood will issue quarterly invoices by consolidating charges and then reconcile monthly usage. Option (a) is much simpler from our billing system perspective.

Open questions for Acme: can you accept monthly invoices with a consolidated quarterly statement for payment? If not, we will need a brief exception from Finance to create a quarterly invoice flow (adds ~2–3 weeks to setup).

I'll put together a capacity table and pricing delta estimate by EOD Tuesday, then share the private offer draft that maps SKUs to committed units.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Marketplace Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — thanks. A couple of finance/legal points to flag before we finalize the private offer template:

- Discounting: For a 40% uplift we're prepared to discuss a stepped discount schedule (tiered by committed spend bands). I will include a proposed schedule in the PO draft.
- Invoicing: Our billing system is optimized around monthly GCP invoices. We can provide a quarterly consolidated statement that lists the three monthly invoices and a single payment reference for your AP team. If Acme mandates one invoice every 90 days, that requires an invoicing exception and an updated payment term in our SOW.
- PO details: Please ensure the PO includes the Redwood legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.), the exact term dates (we should avoid ambiguous "18 months from signature" language) and the HubSpot deal ID (HUB-ACME-2027-118) to speed reconciliation.

Jordan — attaching a draft PO that embeds the stepped discount table and the billing options. Can you confirm the invoice timing requirement and return a countersigned PO (or confirm we should send DocuSign)?

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the quick replies and for sharing the PO. Recap and proposed commitments so we have a single thread of truth: 

1) Term: 18 months, explicit dates 2027-07-01 through 2028-12-31 (not "18 months from signature").
2) Capacity: 40% committed uplift mapped to SKU groups in us-central1 / us-east1; Dev will send SKU table + pricing delta by tomorrow.
3) Billing: Redwood will continue to issue GCP marketplace monthly invoices. We will also generate a quarterly consolidated statement summarizing the three monthly invoices for Acme's AP team to remit a single payment per quarter. This avoids an invoicing-exception.
4) Discounts: Marissa to include a stepped discount table in the private offer.
5) Execution: Once Acme confirms acceptance of monthly invoices + quarterly consolidated statement, Marissa will produce a DocuSign-ready PO that includes the HubSpot deal id. We aim to have the DocuSign envelope out by 2027-05-21 to meet a 2027-07-01 start.

Action owners and ETA:
- Dev: SKU/pricing table and capped burst recommendation — 2027-05-19 EOD.
- Marissa: DocuSign-ready PO + discount bands — 2027-05-20 midday.
- Jordan / Acme: Confirm invoice timing (monthly + consolidated quarterly statement OK?) and return countersigned PO or confirm DocuSign path — 2027-05-20 EOD.

If that timeline works I'll lock it in and then push the private offer into GCP once we have countersignature. Appreciate the partnership — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
